title: Per-constituent index contribution (market_data/index_contributions/{index}/{date}.json, v1)
description: Producer: collectors/index_contributions.py::collect (alpha-engine-config-I11297). Joins per-constituent index weight (collectors/constituents.py for SPX, market_data/index_constituents/NDX.json for NDX) with per-name daily returns from the ArcticDB universe library, so a consumer can explain an index's daily move by name. Consumer: metron (api/services/benchmark_gap.py, metron-ops-I346), which reads latest.json to decompose the holdings-vs-benchmark return gap. Carries an explicit payload schema_version, unlike the older constituents.json contract. UNITS, stated because a consumer already reverse-engineered the wrong convention from an inconsistent worked example: `weight_prior_close` is the ONLY fraction in this artifact. `return_pct` and `index_return_pct` are PERCENT (28.8 means +28.8%). `contribution_pp`, `explained_pp` and `residual_pp` are PERCENTAGE POINTS. Percent and percentage points are the same numeric scale, so EVERY field except `weight_prior_close` divides by 100 to become a fraction -- there is no mixed convention. The identity is `weight_prior_close x return_pct = contribution_pp`: 0.0121 x 28.8 = 0.348.

proxy_symbol.description: The TRADEABLE ETF proxy whose close-to-close move `index_return_pct` is. The index values ^GSPC/^IXIC/^NDX/^RUT carry a separate index licence, which is why the fleet carries proxies; this field travels with the number so a consumer cannot misattribute the proxy's move to the index itself.

prior_close_date.description: The previous TRADING day, read off the proxy's own observed series rather than a calendar. Contribution to the move is prior-close weight times the return between these two dates, so a consumer that recomputes must use this pair and not infer one.

index_return_pct.description: The proxy's close-to-close move in PERCENT (2.0 means +2.0%), not a fraction.

weight_method.description: Weight provenance carried unchanged from the weight producer. The Nasdaq-100 weights read 'modified_cap_approx' until a licensed feed lands; an approximation that does not travel with its data gets absorbed as fact, so a consumer must render this rather than infer it.

residual_pp.description: index_return_pct minus explained_pp, NAMED rather than hidden in rounding. The sum never ties exactly: cash and futures rows carry index weight the equity roster cannot account for, members with no return sit here, and approximate weights contribute error. A consumer reconciling against this artifact needs the gap stated.

explained_pp.description: Sum of contribution_pp, in PERCENTAGE POINTS.

weight_with_return.description: Fraction of index weight for which a return was actually available. The producer refuses to publish below its coverage floor, so a consumer can trust this is above it — but must still render it, because a component emitting nothing is not healthy and neither is one whose coverage silently slipped.

members_missing_return.description: Members whose return was unavailable for this session. They are NOT given a zero contribution -- their weight falls into residual_pp, where it stays visible.

weight_prior_close.description: Index weight at the PRIOR close, as a FRACTION in [0,1]. The only fraction in this artifact.

return_pct.description: The constituent's close-to-close move in PERCENT (28.8 means +28.8%), not a fraction. Divide by 100 for a fraction-domain return.

contribution_pp.description: weight_prior_close x return_pct, in PERCENTAGE POINTS. Divide by 100 for the fraction-domain contribution the shared attribution library works in.

fetched_at.description: Wall-clock stamp of the run, not a data value (alpha-engine-config-I10894): shadow/parity.py excludes it from `values.breaches` and reports it under `provenance_diffs`, because a shadow run and its live counterpart never run at the same instant.

trading_day.description: The trading session this decomposition describes. Named `trading_day` rather than `as_of` deliberately: across the fleet `as_of` names a RUN timestamp and is declared x-provenance so a re-production is not graded as a mismatch. This is a DATA value — re-producing a given session must yield the same date, and a shadow run that produced the WRONG day must be flagged rather than excluded from comparison. `fetched_at` remains the sole provenance field.
